long_biography.plain_text:
Construction took hold of Art Favre in Gulfport, where he worked for a home builder during high school and watched buildings rise from bare ground. After graduating in LSU's first construction-management class in 1972, he learned large-project contracting at Lurgi-Knost, Fluor and Universal.

At Performance, Favre and his partner handled bidding, payroll and tax deposits themselves while the young firm pursued small lump-sum jobs. Repeat work eventually carried it into major industrial projects across the United States. Favre later handed day-to-day leadership to Kevin Courville and became chairman. His philanthropy includes a $15 million gift for LSU's planned Construction and Advanced Manufacturing Building, and he has led fundraising for the project.
